concepts.title: Matrix Order and Elements
concepts.definition: A matrix's dimensions are defined by the count of its horizontal rows and vertical columns, expressed as m x n.
concepts.key_idea: The total count of entries in a matrix is the product of its row and column counts.
question_patterns: what is the order of a matrix with m rows and n columns
calculate the number of elements in a 3x4 matrix
find the possible orders for a matrix having 8 elements
how many entries are in a matrix of order m by n
Explain the method of Matrix Order and Elements.

solution_steps.explain: Determine the number of rows (m) and columns (n).

solution_steps.action: List all factor pairs of the total
solution_steps.explain: Find all pairs of positive integers (m, n) such that m * n equals the total number of elements.
solution_steps.compute: factor_pairs = [(m, n) for m in range(1, total+1) for n in range(1, total+1) if m * n == total]

solution_steps.action: State each factor pair as a possible order
solution_steps.explain: Each pair (m, n) represents a valid matrix order m x n, giving all possible orders for the given element count.

concepts.title: Matrix Construction from General Element Formula
concepts.definition: Creating a matrix by calculating each entry a_ij based on its specific row index i and column index j using a given mathematical rule.
concepts.key_idea: Substitute the row and column position into the provided expression to find each entry.
question_patterns: construct a 2x2 matrix where a_ij = (i+j)^2 / 2
find the elements of a 3x2 matrix given the formula for a_ij
generate a matrix based on the rule a_ij = i/j
write the matrix of order 2x2 where entries are defined by i and j
Explain the method of Matrix Construction from General Element Formula.

solution_steps.action: Calculate element at row i and column j
solution_steps.explain: Apply the given formula using the specific indices i and j.

solution_steps.action: Repeat the calculation for every position in the matrix
solution_steps.explain: Iterate over all row indices i from 1 to m and column indices j from 1 to n, computing each entry using the same formula.

solution_steps.action: Assemble all computed values into the final matrix
solution_steps.explain: Arrange the computed entries in their respective positions to form the complete m x n matrix.
solution_steps.compute: matrix = [[entry_ij for j in range(cols)] for i in range(rows)]

concepts.title: Equality of Matrices
concepts.definition: Two matrices are identical if they share the same dimensions and every entry in one matches the entry at the same position in the other.
concepts.key_idea: Corresponding elements must be equal for the matrices to be equal.
question_patterns: find the values of x and y if the matrices are equal
solve for variables by equating corresponding matrix elements
given A = B, determine the unknown constants
compare two matrices to find missing values
Explain the method of Equality of Matrices.

solution_steps.explain: Set the expression at position (i,j) in the first matrix equal to the value at (i,j) in the second.

solution_steps.action: Solve each equation for the unknown variable
solution_steps.explain: Isolate the unknown in each resulting equation to determine its numerical value.
Substitute the found values back into both matrices and confirm every corresponding entry is equal.
solution_steps.compute: is_equal = all(a_ij == b_ij for all positions)

concepts.title: Matrix Addition and Subtraction
concepts.definition: The sum or difference of two matrices of the same order is found by adding or subtracting their corresponding elements.
concepts.key_idea: Addition is only possible for matrices with identical dimensions.
question_patterns: find the sum of matrices A and B
calculate A + B given two matrices
subtract matrix B from matrix A
compute the result of A - B
Explain the method of Matrix Addition and Subtraction.

solution_steps.explain: Sum the values at the same row and column index from both matrices.

solution_steps.action: Repeat for every position in the matrices
solution_steps.explain: Iterate over all row and column indices, applying the same addition (or subtraction) to each pair of corresponding entries.
Arrange all computed sums (or differences) in their respective positions to form the final m x n result matrix.
solution_steps.compute: result = [[a_ij + b_ij for j in range(cols)] for i in range(rows)]

concepts.title: Scalar Multiplication
concepts.definition: Multiplying every single entry of a matrix by a constant real number or function.
concepts.key_idea: The scalar scales every element in the matrix uniformly.
question_patterns: multiply matrix A by the scalar k
find 3A if A is a given matrix
calculate the negative of a matrix
compute 2A - B
Explain the method of Scalar Multiplication.

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the specific matrix entry by the scalar constant k.

solution_steps.action: Repeat for every element in the matrix
solution_steps.explain: Apply the scalar multiplication to each entry across all rows and columns so the entire matrix is scaled uniformly.
Arrange all scaled entries in their original positions to form the final m x n matrix kA.
solution_steps.compute: scaled_matrix = [[k * a_ij for j in range(cols)] for i in range(rows)]

concepts.title: Matrix Multiplication Condition
concepts.definition: The product AB exists only if the number of columns in the first matrix equals the number of rows in the second matrix.
concepts.key_idea: Inner dimensions must match for multiplication to be defined.
question_patterns: is the product AB defined for these matrices
check if matrix multiplication is possible
what is the order of the product matrix AB
determine if BA can be calculated
Explain the method of Matrix Multiplication Condition.

solution_steps.explain: Count the columns in the first matrix.
Count the rows in the second matrix.
If columns of A equals rows of B, the product is defined.

concepts.title: Transpose of a Matrix
concepts.definition: A new matrix formed by switching the rows and columns of the original matrix.
concepts.key_idea: The first row becomes the first column, the second row becomes the second column, and so on.
question_patterns: find the transpose of matrix A
calculate A'
verify that (A')' = A
write the transpose of the given 3x2 matrix
Explain the method of Transpose of a Matrix.

solution_steps.explain: Take the elements of the first row and write them as the first column of the new matrix.

solution_steps.action: Repeat for every row of the original matrix
solution_steps.explain: Continue converting each subsequent row into its corresponding column so that the i-th row becomes the i-th column.
Combine all converted columns to form the complete transpose A', whose dimensions are n x m for an m x n original.

concepts.title: Symmetric and Skew-Symmetric Matrices
concepts.definition: A square matrix is symmetric if it equals its transpose, and skew-symmetric if its transpose equals its negative.
concepts.key_idea: Symmetric matrices are mirrored across the diagonal; skew-symmetric matrices have zeros on the diagonal.
question_patterns: show that the matrix is symmetric
verify if A is a skew-symmetric matrix
check the symmetry of the given square matrix
prove that A + A' is symmetric
Explain the method of Symmetric and Skew-Symmetric Matrices.

solution_steps.explain: Calculate A' by interchanging rows and columns.
Check if A' is equal to A or -A.
If A' equals A, the matrix is symmetric; if A' equals -A, it is skew-symmetric; otherwise it is neither.

concepts.title: Decomposition into Symmetric and Skew-Symmetric Parts
concepts.definition: Every square matrix can be uniquely split into the sum of one symmetric matrix and one skew-symmetric matrix.
concepts.key_idea: The symmetric part is the average of A and its transpose; the skew-symmetric part is half their difference.
question_patterns: express the matrix as a sum of symmetric and skew-symmetric matrices
find the symmetric part of matrix A
decompose a square matrix into its symmetric and skew components
write A as P + Q where P is symmetric and Q is skew-symmetric
Explain the method of Decomposition into Symmetric and Skew-Symmetric Parts.

solution_steps.action: Verify the decomposition A = P + Q
solution_steps.explain: Add the symmetric and skew-symmetric parts to confirm their sum reconstructs the original matrix A.
